applied_text: // prob[k] = exp(log_unnorm[k] - max_log) / sum_exp == exp(log_unnorm[k] - log_total);
text: In AdjacentCategoryLogitNegLogLik::operator() each row calls exp() 2K times plus log() once: K times for the log-sum-exp terms and then K more times to recompute the same terms shifted by log(sum_exp). This change stores the first pass's exp(log_unnorm[k] - max_log) in prob[k] and then divides by sum_exp. Mathematically exp(a - max - log S) = exp(a - max) / S. sum_exp >= 1 always, because the max term is exp(0) = 1, so the division is safe. This removes K of the 2K+1 libm calls per row and makes the normalisation loop a plain division loop, which GCC can vectorise with SSE2 divpd at baseline x86-64. log(sum_exp) is still computed because neg_ll needs log_total.

applied_text: // ei in (1e-8, 1 - 1e-8): both logs are finite and nonzero, so a zero coefficient adds exactly 0.
text: loglik_from_eta (inlined into fit_constrained_binomial_cpp_impl, and run on every step-halving probe of every IRLS iteration) works out both terms of y*a + (1-y)*b for every row. For binary y, one of the two coefficients is exactly zero, so one libm call per row (log1p(-exp(ei)) on the log link, so two calls; log or log1p on the identity link) is computed and then multiplied by zero. The change skips the zero-coefficient term when y[i] is exactly 1 (or, on the identity link, exactly 0) and keeps the original expression for every other y, including fractional and NaN values. For a log-link fit with a y mean of about 0.3, this removes about 30% of the exp+log1p pairs in the line search. The line search is most of the per-iteration libm work: the mu/w update does n exp calls, and each probe does n exp plus n log1p.
